I am a 57-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with 20 years of experience. My family has 8 people, and some of my children work in factories in the city, so I do not have as much labor at home as I used to. My farm is 14 mu with well irrigation, which means I can water when I need to, but I must pay for the electricity. I grow cotton, wheat, and maize. The wheat and maize are on rotation — wheat in winter, maize in summer on the same 8 mu. I keep 6 mu for cotton because cotton prices have been acceptable and I know how to grow it, but it needs many pesticide sprays and my back is not what it used to be, so I do not want more.

For **wheat**, I will sow improved seed in early October after rotary tillage. I apply compound fertilizer as basal and urea at green-up. I irrigate four times — including the winter irrigation, which is important for the crop to survive the cold and establish strong roots. I spray pesticides four times for aphids and diseases. I expect about 1000 kg per mu.

For **maize**, I plant hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble right after harvest in early June — no tillage, just like my neighbors do. It saves time and fuel. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate three times during the summer when it gets hot and dry. I spray three times for borers and weeds. I expect about 1100 kg per mu.

For **cotton**, I rotary till in April and plant improved seed. I apply compound fertilizer as basal and topdress once more during flowering. Cotton is the most troublesome — bollworms, aphids, and mites never stop, so I spray 16 times through the season. I irrigate three times. I expect about 550 kg per mu. I keep the cotton area at 6 mu because more would be too much work for me and my wife now that our children are away.
